Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

by preposition

the doer, with a passive verb

also done by, made by, written by, loved by

classical

Cic. Att. 1.5.8: tē ā mē frāternē amārī
Mart. 5.84.2: clāmōsō revocātur ā magistrō

ā, ab + abl.

preposition with the ablative, after a passive verb; ā before consonants, ab before vowels and h

by (a person or an animal)

Only for a person, or a creature thought of as acting: ā cane … tenētur aper. A thing or a force that does it stands in the plain ablative, without ā (see “by”, the means): vīpera necat morsū.

Other words

  • cāsus datīvus — by (the person who has to do something)

    construction: the person in the dative, with the gerundive · also used · classical · Caes. BG 2.20.1: Caesarī omnia ūnō tempore erant agenda

    With the gerundive Latin names the doer in the dative, not with ā: mihi eundum est, I have to go.

Examples

  • cūrā ut valeās et nōs amēs et tibi persuādeās tē ā mē frāternē amārī

    take care of yourself, love us, and be sure that you are loved by me like a brotherCic. Att. 1.5.8

  • jam trīstis nucibus puer relictīs clāmōsō revocātur ā magistrō

    now the boy sadly leaves his nuts and is called back by the shouting schoolmasterMart. 5.84.1–2

  • parva necat morsū spatiōsum vīpera taurum: ā cane nōn magnō saepe tenētur aper

    a small viper kills a huge bull with its bite; a boar is often held by a dog of no great sizeOv. Rem. 421–422

  • quōcumque diēī tempore inclāmātus ā puerō, quamvīs occultus atque abditus, ex īmō advolābat

    at whatever time of day he was called by the boy, however hidden and out of sight, he came flying up from the depthsPlin. NH 9.25

  • Caesarī omnia ūnō tempore erant agenda

    Caesar had everything to do at onceCaes. BG 2.20.1

See also by.
